text.title: What happens after an actual EMA6–pivot crossing?
text.description:
Measure directional price displacement after an actual EMA6 crossing at complete 15-, 30- and 60-minute horizons. Positive means movement in the crossing direction; the event-close price is the reference.

Thirty minutes is the protocol's primary horizon. Paths extending beyond RTH or with missing evidence remain unavailable, and earlier extremes of the signal candle are excluded.
text.finding: Across 1,790 complete 30-minute paths on 636 days, mean directional displacement was -0.04 ES points and 48.8% ended strictly positive. Another 96 candidate paths were unavailable. The selected crossing alone did not produce a positive average 30-minute directional displacement in this sample.

text.title: How far does price travel in either direction after the crossing?
text.description:
For complete 30-minute paths, calculate favorable and adverse excursions from the crossing close and the share reaching 5, 10 or 20 ES points in each direction.

Both directions can be reached in the same path. Minute-bar extremes do not establish which threshold traded first, a fill price or net profitability.
text.finding: The 1,790 complete paths had mean favorable excursion of 9.04 ES points and mean adverse excursion of 8.65 points. The share reaching 10 favorable points was 30.8%, while 30.6% reached 10 adverse points. Excursion opportunity and adverse exposure coexist; the chart does not encode threshold ordering or a trading result.

text.title: How often does EMA6 avoid recrossing the pivot for 30 minutes?
text.description:
Track the next reverse actual EMA6 crossing after each EMA6–pivot event. A complete 30-minute RTH window is required to classify absence of a recross.

Incomplete windows remain censored even when a reverse crossing is observed before the boundary. An EMA6 recross is distinct from a price return through the pivot.
text.finding: No reverse EMA6 crossing occurred in 1,110 of 1,790 complete windows (62.0%), on 636 supporting days. Another 96 windows were censored. Remaining on the same pivot side for 30 minutes does not establish a favorable price displacement or profitable trade.

text.title: Does follow-through differ between first and later crossings?
text.description:
Compare complete 30-minute directional displacement after the first, second and third-or-later actual EMA6–pivot crossings of each RTH session.

Ordinals are known at the event close. Horizon availability remains specific to each event; a late crossing is not assigned a shorter window to complete the table.
text.finding: Mean 30-minute directional displacement was -0.18 ES points after first crossings (636 complete paths), 0.69 after second crossings, and -0.33 after third-or-later crossings. The table retains the different support and unavailable-path counts. These exploratory ordinal groups are not independent replications or a selected trading rule.

text.title: How often does price retest the pivot after an EMA6 crossing?
text.description:
Look for the first subsequent completed three-minute bar containing the exact pivot within 30 minutes of an actual EMA6–pivot crossing. Complete windows determine retest incidence; observed touches separately support close classifications.

The touch definition uses bar ranges and does not infer an intrabar fill, a limit-order execution or the quality of a retest entry.
text.finding: A retest occurred in 1,134 of 1,790 complete windows (63.4%), supported by 636 days. Another 96 incidence windows were censored. A pivot revisit is a frequent-path description under this bar-based definition; it does not measure whether a retest trade would have filled or made money.
